recipes.name: Classic Beef Chilli
recipes.method:
Heat the oil in a large pot and soften the diced onions for 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and diced peppers and cook for 3 more minutes.
Add the beef mince and brown all over, breaking it up as you go.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, chilli powder and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and stock, bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain and add the kidney beans, simmer 10 more minutes.
Season to taste and serve with rice, or cool and portion for the freezer.
recipes.notes: Even better the next day. Freezes for 3 months.

recipes.name: Slow Bolognese Ragu
recipes.method:
Heat the oil and fry the lardons until golden.
Add finely diced onion, carrot and celery and soften for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, then the mince, and brown well.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add tomatoes, stock and oregano, then simmer very gently, partially covered, for 90 minutes.
Stir in the milk for the last 10 minutes and season well.
Serve with pasta, or portion and freeze.
recipes.notes: The milk softens the acidity. Makes a generous 5 portions of sauce.

recipes.name: Cottage Pie
recipes.method:
Brown the mince in a large pan, then remove and set aside.
Soften the diced onion and carrot for 8 minutes.
Return the mince, stir in the flour and tomato puree, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add stock and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 25 minutes, adding the peas at the end.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with butter and milk.
Spoon the mince into a baking dish, top with mash and grated cheddar.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes: Assemble ahead and freeze unbaked, then cook from defrosted.

recipes.name: Lamb & Apricot Tagine
recipes.method:
Brown the lamb in batches in the oil and set aside.
Soften the sliced onions for 8 minutes, add garlic and ras el hanout and cook 1 minute.
Return the lamb with tomatoes, stock, honey and halved apricots.
Cover and simmer very gently for 90 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the drained chickpeas for the final 15 minutes.
Scatter with flaked almonds and serve with couscous.
recipes.notes: Slow cooker friendly: 6 hours on low.

recipes.name: Chicken & Chorizo Traybake
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Halve the potatoes and parboil for 8 minutes, then drain.
Toss potatoes, sliced peppers, onion wedges and whole garlic cloves in oil and paprika in a large roasting tray.
Nestle in the chicken thighs skin-side up and sliced chorizo.
Roast for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the skin crisp.
Add the cherry tomatoes for the final 10 minutes.
recipes.notes: Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge and reheat well.

recipes.name: Coconut Chicken Curry
recipes.method:
Soften the sliced onions in oil for 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, curry powder and turmeric and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the diced chicken and coat in the spices.
Pour in the coconut milk and tomatoes and simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir through the spinach until wilted and season.
Serve with rice and portion the rest for the freezer.
recipes.notes: Use light coconut milk for a lighter version.

recipes.name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.method:
Brown the chicken thighs in oil on both sides and set aside.
Soften the sliced onion, pepper and mushrooms for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and oregano and cook 1 minute.
Return the chicken, add tomatoes, stock and olives.
Simmer partially covered for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Serve with pasta, rice or crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Bone-in thighs give the best flavour.

recipes.name: Creamy Chicken & Leek Pie Filling
recipes.method:
Brown the diced chicken in half the butter and set aside.
Soften the sliced leeks and mushrooms in the remaining butter for 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually add stock and milk, stirring to a smooth sauce.
Return the chicken with the mustard and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the creme fraiche and season.
Use under puff pastry, with mash, or freeze in portions.
recipes.notes: A versatile base: pie one night, pasta sauce another.

recipes.name: Chicken Fajita Rice Bowls
recipes.method:
Cook the rice and set aside.
Slice the chicken, peppers and onions and toss with the fajita seasoning and oil.
Fry in a hot pan in two batches until charred and cooked through.
Warm the drained black beans.
Divide rice between 5 containers, top with the fajita mix and beans.
Finish with lime juice and a spoon of soured cream when serving.
recipes.notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge for weekday lunches.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
recipes.method:
Mix the paprika, sugar, cumin and garlic granules and rub all over the pork.
Place in the slow cooker with the stock and vinegar.
Cook on low for 8 hours until falling apart.
Shred with two forks, discarding excess fat.
Stir through the BBQ sauce and some cooking juices.
Serve in buns, with rice, or in wraps; freeze the rest flat in bags.
recipes.notes: Also works in the oven: 150C covered for 4 hours.

recipes.name: Sausage & Bean Casserole
recipes.method:
Brown the sausages all over in the oil and set aside.
Soften the diced onion and carrot for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Return the sausages with tomatoes and stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Add the drained beans for the final 10 minutes.
Serve with mash or crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Swap in veggie sausages for a meat-free version.

recipes.name: Family Fish Pie
recipes.method:
Boil the potatoes and mash with a third of the butter.
Soften the sliced leeks in the remaining butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk to a smooth sauce, add mustard and season.
Fold in the fish, prawns and peas and tip into a baking dish.
Top with the mash and grated cheddar.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until bubbling and golden.
recipes.notes: Freeze unbaked; defrost fully before cooking.

recipes.name: Harissa Salmon & Veg Traybake
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Halve the potatoes, toss in half the oil and roast for 20 minutes.
Mix the harissa with the remaining oil and brush over the salmon.
Add peppers and broccoli to the tray, nestle in the salmon.
Roast 15 more minutes until the salmon is just cooked.
Squeeze over lemon and serve with a spoon of yogurt.
recipes.notes: Swap salmon for cod loin if preferred.

recipes.name: Red Lentil Dahl
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onions in oil for 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and the ground spices and fry 2 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and stock.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Wilt in the spinach, season, and finish with garam masala.
Serve with rice or flatbreads.
recipes.notes: Costs roughly £1 a portion. Freezes brilliantly.

recipes.name: Three Bean Veggie Chilli
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion, pepper and carrot in oil for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and all the spices and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, stock and all the drained beans.
Simmer for 30 minutes until rich and thick.
Season and serve with rice, jacket potatoes or nachos.
recipes.notes: A square of dark chocolate stirred in at the end adds depth.

recipes.name: Mushroom Stroganoff
recipes.method:
Fry the sliced mushrooms in batches in the oil until golden and set aside.
Soften the sliced onions in the butter for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Return the mushrooms with the stock and mustard and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the soured cream and warm through without boiling.
Serve with rice, pasta or mash.
recipes.notes: Fridge-friendly for 3 days; the sauce thickens overnight.

recipes.name: Roasted Veg Pasta Sauce
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Chop all the veg into chunks and spread over two trays with the whole garlic cloves.
Toss with oil and oregano and roast for 35 minutes until soft and charred at the edges.
Blend the roasted veg with the chopped tomatoes and balsamic until smooth.
Simmer for 10 minutes and season.
Stir through pasta now and freeze the rest in portions.
recipes.notes: Brilliant for hiding veg from fussy eaters.

recipes.name: Chickpea & Spinach Curry
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onions in oil for 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and curry powder and fry 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, coconut milk and drained chickpeas.
Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Wilt in the spinach and season well.
Serve with rice or naan.
recipes.notes: Pantry-staple friendly; under £1 a portion.

recipes.name: Macaroni Cheese with Hidden Cauliflower
recipes.method:
Cook the macaroni with the cauliflower florets in the same pot until both are tender, then drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk to a smooth sauce.
Stir in most of the cheddar and the mustard off the heat.
Fold in the pasta and cauliflower and tip into a baking dish.
Top with remaining cheese and breadcrumbs and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.
recipes.notes: Blend the cauliflower into the sauce for total invisibility.

recipes.name: Big Batch Minestrone
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion, carrot and celery in oil for 10 minutes.
Add garlic and oregano and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and stock and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the pasta, diced courgette and drained beans and simmer 10 more minutes until the pasta is cooked.
Season generously and serve with grated cheese.
recipes.notes: If freezing, leave the pasta out and add when reheating.

recipes.name: Butternut Squash & Chilli Soup
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Peel and chunk the squash, toss with half the oil and roast for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the diced onion and carrot in the remaining oil.
Add garlic and sliced chilli and cook 1 minute.
Add the roasted squash and stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend until silky, stir in the coconut milk and season.
recipes.notes: Roasting the squash first doubles the flavour.

recipes.name: Leek & Potato Soup
recipes.method:
Soften the sliced leeks and diced onion in the butter for 10 minutes without colouring.
Add the diced potatoes and stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is tender.
Blend until smooth, stir in the milk and season well.
Serve with crusty bread.
recipes.notes: About 60p a portion. Freezes for 3 months.

recipes.name: Lentil Bolognese
recipes.method:
Soften the finely diced onion, carrot and celery in oil for 10 minutes.
Add garlic, chopped mushrooms and oregano and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree, then add lentils, tomatoes and stock.
Simmer for 30 minutes until the lentils are tender, topping up with water if needed.
Season with the soy sauce and black pepper.
Serve with spaghetti.
recipes.notes: The soy sauce adds savoury depth. Cheaper than beef and freezes just as well.

recipes.name: Thai Green Chicken Curry
recipes.method:
Fry the curry paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the diced chicken and coat in the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the green beans and baby corn and cook 8 more minutes.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime juice to balance.
Serve with jasmine rice.
recipes.notes: Shop-bought paste keeps it quick; add more for heat.

recipes.name: Egg Fried Rice with Peas
recipes.method:
Cook the rice, then cool it (ideally use cold leftover rice).
Beat the eggs and scramble in a little oil, then set aside.
Fry the sliced spring onions and garlic in the remaining oil for 1 minute.
Add the peas and rice and stir-fry over high heat for 4 minutes.
Return the egg, add the soy sauce and toss through.
Serve hot.
recipes.notes: A great way to use up leftover rice. Add any veg lurking in the fridge.

recipes.name: Jacket Potatoes with Tuna Mayo
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Prick the potatoes, rub with a little oil and salt, and bake for 1 hour until crisp.
Mix the drained tuna with mayonnaise, drained sweetcorn and sliced spring onions.
Split the baked potatoes and fill with the tuna mayo.
Top with grated cheddar to serve.
recipes.notes: Bake potatoes in bulk and reheat through the week.

recipes.name: Spiced Carrot & Lentil Soup
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion in oil for 5 minutes.
Add the cumin and chilli flakes and cook 1 minute.
Add the grated carrot, rinsed lentils and stock.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Blend until smooth and season.
Serve with bread.
recipes.notes: Roughly 55p a portion. Doubles easily for the freezer.

recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion, carrot and celery in oil for 10 minutes.
Add garlic and tomato puree and cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, stock and half the beans.
Blend the other half of the beans with a little stock and stir in for creaminess.
Simmer 15 minutes, add the pasta and cook until tender.
Season and serve with olive oil.
recipes.notes: Hearty and filling for under £1 a portion.

recipes.name: Bubble & Squeak Fritters
recipes.method:
Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash roughly.
Shred and fry the cabbage and diced onion in the butter until soft.
Mix the cabbage into the potato with the flour and beaten eggs and season.
Shape into patties.
Fry in oil for 3-4 minutes each side until golden and crisp.
Serve with a fried egg or baked beans.
recipes.notes: Perfect for using up Sunday roast leftovers.

recipes.name: Curried Chickpea Wraps
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion in oil for 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Add the drained chickpeas and tomatoes and simmer 12 minutes, lightly crushing some chickpeas.
Season well.
Warm the wraps, fill with salad leaves and the curried chickpeas, and roll up.
recipes.notes: The filling also keeps for lunchboxes through the week.

recipes.name: Tomato & White Bean Stew
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion in oil for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, stock and drained butter beans.
Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Wilt in the spinach and season.
Serve with crusty bread or rice.
recipes.notes: Add a chilli for heat. Very freezer-friendly.

recipes.name: Cheese & Onion Pasta Bake
recipes.method:
Cook the pasta and drain.
Soften the sliced onions in the butter for 10 minutes until sweet.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk to a smooth sauce.
Stir in most of the cheese and the mustard off the heat.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish, top with remaining cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes.
recipes.notes: Caramelising the onions properly makes all the difference.

recipes.name: Lemon & Herb Chicken Thighs with Orzo
recipes.method:
Brown the chicken thighs skin-side down in an ovenproof pan and set aside.
Soften the diced onion and garlic in the fat for 5 minutes.
Stir in the orzo and oregano, then the stock and lemon zest.
Nestle the chicken back on top and bake at 190C for 25 minutes.
Stir the spinach through the orzo and squeeze over the lemon.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes: Everything cooks in one pan - minimal washing up.

recipes.name: Keema Peas Curry
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onions in oil for 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and the spices and fry 2 minutes.
Add the lamb mince and brown well.
Stir in the tomatoes and a splash of water and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the peas and cook 5 more minutes.
Season and serve with rice or naan.
recipes.notes: Use beef mince for a cheaper version.

recipes.name: Gnocchi with Sausage & Kale
recipes.method:
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins and fry in oil, breaking into pieces, until golden.
Add garlic and chilli flakes and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and a splash of water and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the shredded kale until wilted.
Add the gnocchi and cook per packet, loosening with pasta water.
Finish with grated parmesan.
recipes.notes: On the table in half an hour.

recipes.name: Katsu Chicken Curry
recipes.method:
For the sauce, soften the diced onion and carrot, add garlic and curry powder and cook 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk, stock and honey and simmer 15 minutes, then blend smooth.
Coat the chicken in flour, then beaten egg, then panko.
Shallow fry for 4 minutes each side until golden and cooked.
Serve sliced over rice with the katsu sauce.
recipes.notes: The sauce freezes well; make a double batch.

recipes.name: Smoked Haddock & Spring Onion Fishcakes
recipes.method:
Boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash, then cool.
Poach the haddock in a little water for 5 minutes, then flake, discarding skin and bones.
Mix the fish into the mash with sliced spring onions and mustard and season.
Shape into 10 cakes, then coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry for 3-4 minutes each side until golden.
Serve with peas and a wedge of lemon.
recipes.notes: Freeze uncooked after coating; fry from frozen on a lower heat.

recipes.name: Halloumi & Roasted Veg Couscous
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Chop the veg into chunks, toss with oil and roast for 25 minutes.
Pour the hot stock over the couscous, cover and leave 5 minutes, then fluff.
Fry the sliced halloumi until golden on both sides.
Stir the harissa and roasted veg through the couscous.
Top with the halloumi to serve.
recipes.notes: Great hot or cold for packed lunches.

recipes.name: Beef & Ale Stew with Dumplings
recipes.method:
Toss the beef in the plain flour and brown in batches in oil, then set aside.
Soften the onions, carrots and mushrooms for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree, then the ale, scraping the pan.
Return the beef with the stock, cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes.
Mix the self-raising flour and suet with water to a soft dough and shape into dumplings.
Sit the dumplings on the stew, cover and cook 25 minutes until risen.
recipes.notes: Make the stew ahead; add fresh dumplings when reheating.

recipes.name: Chicken, Leek & Bacon Risotto
recipes.method:
Fry the lardons and diced chicken in oil until golden, then set aside.
Soften the sliced leeks and garlic in the butter for 6 minutes.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until absorbed.
After about 18 minutes the rice should be creamy and tender.
Stir the chicken and bacon back in to warm through.
Finish with parmesan and rest 2 minutes.
recipes.notes: Keep the stock hot in a separate pan for the best texture.

recipes.name: Spinach & Ricotta Cannelloni
recipes.method:
Wilt the spinach, squeeze out the water and chop, then mix with the ricotta, nutmeg and seasoning.
Fry the garlic in oil, add the passata and simmer 5 minutes to make a sauce.
Pipe or spoon the spinach mix into the cannelloni tubes.
Spread some sauce in a dish, lay the tubes on top, cover with remaining sauce.
Top with torn mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 190C for 35 minutes until bubbling.
recipes.notes: Assemble and freeze before baking.

recipes.name: Prawn & Chorizo Linguine
recipes.method:
Cook the linguine until al dente, reserving a cup of pasta water.
Fry the diced chorizo until its oil releases.
Add garlic, chilli flakes and halved tomatoes and cook 3 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook until pink.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water and the lemon juice.
Season and serve.
recipes.notes: The chorizo oil is the flavour - don't drain it.

recipes.name: Aubergine Parmigiana
recipes.method:
Slice the aubergines, brush with oil and griddle or roast at 220C until soft and golden.
Fry the garlic in a little oil, add passata and oregano and simmer 10 minutes.
Layer aubergine, tomato sauce, torn mozzarella and parmesan in a dish, repeating.
Finish with parmesan on top.
Bake at 190C for 30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes: Even better made a day ahead.

recipes.name: Harissa Chicken Traybake with Chickpeas
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Toss the chicken with harissa and half the oil.
Spread the drained chickpeas, onion wedges and peppers in a tray with the rest of the oil.
Sit the chicken on top and roast for 35 minutes.
Add the cherry tomatoes for the last 10 minutes.
Squeeze over lemon and serve with couscous or flatbread.
recipes.notes: The chickpeas crisp up beautifully in the chicken juices.

recipes.name: Meatball Marinara
recipes.method:
Mix the mince with breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic and seasoning, then roll into balls.
Brown the meatballs in oil and set aside.
Soften the diced onion and remaining garlic for 5 minutes.
Add passata and oregano and simmer 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Serve with pasta and grated parmesan.
recipes.notes: Make a double batch of meatballs to freeze raw.

recipes.name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Enchiladas
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Dice and roast the sweet potato in oil for 25 minutes.
Fry the onion with the spices, add half the tomatoes and the drained beans and the roasted sweet potato.
Make a sauce from the rest of the tomatoes with a little water.
Fill the wraps with the bean mix, roll and place seam-down in a dish.
Top with sauce and cheese and bake 20 minutes.
recipes.notes: Assemble and freeze before the final bake.

recipes.name: Honey Mustard Pork Traybake
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Halve the potatoes and roast in oil for 20 minutes.
Mix the mustard and honey.
Add onion wedges, apple wedges and the pork (brushed with the glaze) to the tray.
Roast 20 minutes, adding the broccoli for the final 10.
Spoon over the pan juices to serve.
recipes.notes: Apple and pork are a classic pairing.

recipes.name: Spanish Chicken & Rice (Arroz con Pollo)
recipes.method:
Brown the chicken thighs in oil and set aside.
Fry the sliced chorizo, then soften the onion, peppers and garlic.
Stir in the paprika and rice to coat.
Add the hot stock and return the chicken, skin up.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes without stirring much.
Scatter the peas over and cook 5 more minutes until the rice is tender.
recipes.notes: Let it rest off the heat for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Saag Aloo with Paneer
recipes.method:
Cube and fry the paneer until golden, then set aside.
Parboil the diced potatoes for 6 minutes and drain.
Soften the diced onions in oil, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the potatoes and a splash of water and cook 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then fold the paneer back in.
Serve with rice or naan.
recipes.notes: Use frozen spinach (300g) to save money and prep.

recipes.name: Moussaka
recipes.method:
Slice and roast the aubergines and potatoes in oil at 200C until soft.
Brown the lamb with the onion and garlic, add tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer 20 minutes.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and milk, then beat in the egg off the heat.
Layer potatoes, lamb, aubergine in a dish, then top with the white sauce.
Bake at 190C for 35 minutes until golden.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes: A project, but freezes very well in portions.

recipes.name: Slow Braised Beef Short Rib
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 150C.
Season and brown the short ribs all over in oil in a casserole, then set aside.
Soften the diced onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes, add garlic and tomato puree.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half.
Return the ribs with the stock and thyme, cover and braise for 3 hours until falling off the bone.
Reduce the sauce on the hob if needed and serve over mash.
recipes.notes: Make a day ahead and reheat gently - the flavour deepens. Impressive but mostly hands-off.

recipes.name: Pan-Seared Sea Bass with Salsa Verde
recipes.method:
Boil the baby potatoes until tender and keep warm.
For the salsa verde, finely chop the herbs, capers and garlic and mix with the mustard, lemon juice and most of the oil.
Pat the sea bass dry and season the skin.
Fry skin-side down in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until crisp, then flip for 1 minute.
Serve the fish over the potatoes with salsa verde spooned over.
recipes.notes: Make the salsa verde ahead; cook the fish at the last minute.

recipes.name: Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce
recipes.method:
Score the duck skin and season.
Place skin-side down in a cold pan and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes to render the fat.
Flip and cook 4 minutes, then rest skin-side up under foil.
In the same pan, add cherries, wine, stock, honey and balsamic and reduce to a glossy sauce.
Roast or boil the potatoes and steam the broccoli.
Slice the duck and serve with the cherry sauce.
recipes.notes: Resting the duck is essential for a pink, tender finish.

recipes.name: Mushroom & Truffle Risotto
recipes.method:
Soak the porcini in some of the hot stock for 15 minutes, then chop, keeping the liquid.
Fry the sliced chestnut mushrooms in butter until golden and set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic, stir in the rice for 1 minute, then the wine.
Add hot stock (including the porcini liquid) a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Stir in the mushrooms, parmesan and a knob of butter.
Finish each plate with a drizzle of truffle oil.
recipes.notes: Truffle oil goes a long way - just a few drops per plate.

recipes.name: Rack of Lamb with Herb Crust
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Sear the lamb racks all over in oil until browned.
Blitz the breadcrumbs, herbs and garlic with a little oil.
Brush the lamb with mustard and press on the herb crust.
Roast for 20 minutes for pink, then rest 10 minutes.
Roast potatoes alongside and steam the broccoli.
Carve into cutlets to serve.
recipes.notes: Ask the butcher to french-trim the racks for a neat finish.

recipes.name: Seafood Paella
recipes.method:
Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in oil in a wide pan.
Stir in the rice and saffron to coat.
Add the tomatoes and hot stock and simmer without stirring for 15 minutes.
Nestle in the prawns, mussels and squid and scatter over the peas.
Cook 8 more minutes until the seafood is done and mussels open (discard any that stay shut).
Rest 5 minutes and serve from the pan.
recipes.notes: A showstopper served straight from the pan at the table.

recipes.name: Beef Wellington (Individual)
recipes.method:
Cut the fillet into 5 portions, sear all over and brush with mustard, then cool.
Blitz and fry the mushrooms with garlic until dry to make a duxelles, then cool.
Lay out prosciutto, spread with duxelles, wrap around each beef portion.
Wrap each in puff pastry, seal and brush with beaten egg.
Chill 20 minutes, then bake at 200C for 20 minutes for medium-rare.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes: Individual Wellingtons are far easier to cook evenly than one large one.

recipes.name: Miso Glazed Salmon
recipes.method:
Mix the miso, honey, soy and grated ginger into a glaze.
Brush over the salmon and leave 10 minutes.
Grill or bake the salmon at 200C for 12 minutes, basting once.
Cook the rice and steam the pak choi.
Scatter the salmon with sesame seeds and serve over rice.
recipes.notes: The glaze caramelises beautifully under a hot grill.

recipes.name: Wild Mushroom Beef Stroganoff
recipes.method:
Sear the beef strips quickly in half the butter over high heat and set aside.
Fry the mushrooms in the rest of the butter until golden.
Add the onion and garlic and soften, then the paprika.
Pour in the brandy and let it bubble, then add stock and mustard.
Stir in the soured cream and warm gently.
Return the beef to just heat through and serve with rice or pappardelle.
recipes.notes: Don't boil once the cream is in, or it can split.

recipes.name: Roast Pork Belly with Apple Sauce
recipes.method:
Score the pork skin, rub with salt and fennel seeds, and leave uncovered in the fridge to dry.
Sit the pork on sliced onions in a tray, add stock, and roast at 160C for 2.5 hours.
Turn the oven to 220C for 30 minutes to crackle the skin.
Simmer peeled apple chunks with a splash of water until soft for the sauce.
Roast the potatoes and steam the broccoli.
Rest the pork, then carve and serve with apple sauce.
recipes.notes: Drying the skin overnight is the secret to perfect crackling.

recipes.name: Chicken Shawarma Bowls
recipes.method:
Mix the spices, garlic, lemon juice and oil and toss with the chicken; marinate 20 minutes.
Roast the chicken at 210C for 25 minutes until charred at the edges, then slice.
Cook the rice.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes for a quick salad.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, salad and a dollop of yogurt.
recipes.notes: Marinate overnight for even better flavour. Great for lunches.

recipes.name: Butternut Squash & Sage Risotto
recipes.method:
Roast half the diced squash at 200C until caramelised.
Dice and soften the rest with the onion in butter, add garlic.
Stir in the rice, then the wine.
Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes until creamy.
Mash the softened squash into the rice and fold in the roasted pieces.
Fry sage leaves in butter and scatter over with parmesan.
recipes.notes: The two ways with squash give creaminess and texture.

recipes.name: Cod & Chorizo Stew
recipes.method:
Fry the diced chorizo until its oil releases.
Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the chorizo oil.
Add paprika, tomatoes and drained butter beans and simmer 15 minutes.
Nestle in chunks of cod, cover and poach for 8 minutes until just cooked.
Season and serve with crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Any firm white fish works here.

recipes.name: Black Bean & Sweetcorn Quesadillas
recipes.method:
Fry the diced onion with the spices, add the drained beans and sweetcorn and lightly crush.
Lay a tortilla in a dry pan, scatter with the bean mix and cheese, top with another tortilla.
Cook 2 minutes each side until crisp and the cheese melts.
Repeat for the rest.
Cut into wedges and serve with salad or soured cream.
recipes.notes: A reliable crowd-pleaser for kids and adults alike.

recipes.name: Butter Chicken
recipes.method:
Marinate the diced chicken in the yogurt, half the garlic and ginger, and the spices for 20 minutes.
Fry the chicken in the butter until coloured.
Add the rest of the garlic and ginger, then the passata, and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in the cream and warm gently.
Serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Milder than most curries - good for the whole family.

recipes.name: Lamb Rogan Josh
recipes.method:
Brown the lamb in oil in batches and set aside.
Soften the sliced onions, add garlic, ginger and the paste and fry 2 minutes.
Return the lamb with the tomatoes and stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes until tender.
Stir in the yogurt at the end off the heat.
Serve with rice and naan.
recipes.notes: Long slow cooking makes the lamb meltingly tender.

recipes.name: Falafel & Flatbread Plate
recipes.method:
Blitz the drained chickpeas with the onion, garlic, parsley, cumin and flour to a coarse paste (do not over-process).
Shape into small patties.
Shallow fry for 3 minutes each side until crisp and golden.
Warm the flatbreads.
Serve the falafel in flatbreads with cucumber and yogurt.
recipes.notes: Use tinned chickpeas, not soaked, for an easy weeknight version.

recipes.name: Chicken & Sweetcorn Soup
recipes.method:
Simmer the chicken in the stock for 12 minutes, then remove and shred.
Add the ginger, garlic and most of the sweetcorn to the stock.
Blend a little of the soup with the rest of the sweetcorn and stir back in for body.
Mix the cornflour with water and stir in to thicken.
Return the chicken, then slowly pour in the beaten eggs, stirring to make ribbons.
Finish with soy sauce and sliced spring onions.
recipes.notes: A comforting, cheap soup that freezes well without the egg.

recipes.name: Chilli Con Carne Loaded Fries
recipes.method:
Brown the mince with the diced onion and garlic.
Stir in the spices, then the tomatoes and drained beans, and simmer 30 minutes.
Meanwhile bake the chips per packet until crisp.
Pile the chips into a dish, spoon over the chilli and scatter with cheese.
Return to the oven for 5 minutes to melt.
Top with soured cream to serve.
recipes.notes: A fun way to stretch a chilli to feed a crowd.

recipes.name: Creamy Tomato & Mascarpone Pasta
recipes.method:
Cook the pasta until al dente.
Soften the diced onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes.
Add the passata and basil and simmer 8 minutes.
Stir in the mascarpone until silky.
Toss the pasta through with a splash of pasta water.
Serve with grated parmesan.
recipes.notes: Mascarpone makes it luxurious for very little money.

recipes.name: Jerk Chicken with Rice & Peas
recipes.method:
Rub the chicken with the jerk seasoning and oil and marinate 20 minutes.
Roast at 200C for 35 minutes until charred and cooked.
For the rice and peas, simmer the rice with the coconut milk, drained beans, spring onions, garlic and thyme plus 300ml water.
Cover and cook 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Serve the chicken over the rice and peas.
recipes.notes: Marinate overnight for the best flavour and a spicier kick.

recipes.name: Tuna Pasta Bake
recipes.method:
Cook the pasta and drain.
Soften the diced onion in the butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the milk to a smooth sauce and stir in most of the cheese.
Fold in the pasta, drained tuna and sweetcorn.
Tip into a dish, top with remaining cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes: A storecupboard hero. Freezes well in portions.

recipes.name: Shakshuka
recipes.method:
Soften the sliced onion and peppers in oil for 10 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Make wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook gently for 6-8 minutes until the whites are set but yolks runny.
Serve from the pan with crusty bread.
recipes.notes: A brilliant any-time-of-day meal for around £1 a head.

recipes.name: Steak Fajitas
recipes.method:
Rub the steak with half the fajita seasoning.
Sear in a hot pan for 2-3 minutes each side, then rest and slice thinly.
Fry the sliced peppers and onions with the rest of the seasoning until charred but still crisp.
Warm the tortillas.
Serve the steak and peppers with lime, soured cream and tortillas for everyone to build their own.
recipes.notes: Resting and slicing the steak against the grain keeps it tender.

recipes.name: Sausage & Mash with Onion Gravy
recipes.method:
Roast or fry the sausages until browned and cooked through.
Boil the potatoes and mash with butter and milk.
Slowly fry the sliced onions in oil for 15 minutes until golden and sweet.
Stir the flour into the onions, then gradually add the stock to make a gravy.
Simmer 5 minutes and season.
Serve the sausages on the mash with plenty of gravy.
recipes.notes: The slow-cooked onions make the gravy - don't rush them.

recipes.name: Vegetable Chow Mein
recipes.method:
Cook the noodles per packet, drain and toss in the sesame oil.
Stir-fry the julienned carrot and sliced pepper in hot oil for 2 minutes.
Add shredded cabbage and garlic and fry 2 more minutes.
Add the noodles, beansprouts and soy sauce.
Toss over high heat for 2 minutes and serve.
recipes.notes: Use up any veg in the fridge - it all works.

recipes.name: Spanish Tortilla
recipes.method:
Thinly slice the potatoes and onions.
Gently fry them in the oil for 15 minutes until soft but not coloured, then drain.
Beat the eggs, season, and stir in the potatoes and onions.
Pour back into the pan and cook on low for 8 minutes until nearly set.
Flip with a plate and cook 3 more minutes.
Rest and serve warm or cold in wedges.
recipes.notes: Brilliant for lunchboxes - keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Pea & Mint Soup
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion in oil for 5 minutes.
Add the diced potato and stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the peas and cook 3 minutes only, to keep them bright.
Add the mint leaves and blend until smooth.
Season and serve hot or chilled.
recipes.notes: Frozen peas make this absurdly cheap and vividly green.

recipes.name: Loaded Bean Nachos
recipes.method:
Fry the diced onion with the spices, add the drained beans and tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Spread the tortilla chips over a large tray.
Spoon over the bean mix and scatter with grated cheese.
Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until melted.
Serve with soured cream.
recipes.notes: Add jalapeños and guacamole if the budget stretches.

recipes.name: Coronation Chickpea Pittas
recipes.method:
Roughly crush the drained chickpeas with a fork.
Mix with the mayonnaise, yogurt, curry powder, chutney and sultanas.
Season to taste.
Toast and split the pittas.
Fill with salad leaves and the coronation chickpeas.
recipes.notes: The filling keeps 3 days - a great fridge standby.

recipes.name: Tomato & Basil Risotto
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion and garlic in the oil and half the butter.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Add the passata, then hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes.
When creamy and tender, beat in the rest of the butter and the parmesan.
Tear in the basil and season.
recipes.notes: Storecupboard comfort at just over £1 a head.

recipes.name: Gnocchi & Tomato Bake
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion and garlic in oil.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the gnocchi straight from the packet.
Tip into a baking dish and top with torn mozzarella.
Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden and bubbling.
recipes.notes: No need to boil the gnocchi first - it cooks in the sauce.

recipes.name: Broccoli & Cheddar Soup
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion in the butter.
Add the diced potato and stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets and chopped stalks and simmer 8 minutes.
Blend until smooth.
Stir in the grated cheddar off the heat and season.
recipes.notes: Use the broccoli stalks too - they're free flavour.

recipes.name: Bacon & Pea Pasta
recipes.method:
Cook the pasta, adding the peas for the final 2 minutes, then drain, keeping a cup of water.
Fry the lardons until crisp, adding the garlic at the end.
Stir in the creme fraiche and a splash of pasta water.
Toss the pasta and peas through the sauce.
Finish with parmesan and black pepper.
recipes.notes: Dinner in under half an hour for about £1.30 a head.

recipes.name: Vegetable Biryani
recipes.method:
Fry the sliced onions in oil until golden, removing half for the topping.
Add the spices, cauliflower florets and diced carrot and coat well.
Stir in the rinsed rice, then the stock and sultanas.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, adding the peas near the end.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes, fluff, and top with the reserved onions.
recipes.notes: A complete meal in one pot.

recipes.name: Corned Beef Hash
recipes.method:
Dice and parboil the potatoes for 8 minutes, then drain well.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until golden.
Add the potatoes and fry until crisp at the edges.
Stir in the cubed corned beef and Worcestershire sauce and heat through.
Top each portion with a fried egg.
recipes.notes: A tinned classic that still earns its place.

recipes.name: Rice & Bean Burritos
recipes.method:
Cook the rice.
Fry the diced onion with the spices, add the beans and tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Mix the rice into the beans.
Fill the wraps with the mix and grated cheese, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Toast seam-down in a dry pan for 2 minutes each side.
recipes.notes: Wrap in foil and freeze; reheat in the oven from frozen.

recipes.name: Potato & Chickpea Curry
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onions in oil, add garlic and curry powder.
Add the diced potatoes and coat in the spices.
Add tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer 20 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the drained chickpeas for the final 5 minutes.
Season and serve with rice or naan.
recipes.notes: 90p a portion and deeply satisfying.

recipes.name: Garlic Mushroom Spaghetti
recipes.method:
Cook the spaghetti, reserving a cup of pasta water.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in oil over high heat until deeply golden.
Add the butter and sliced garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water, lemon juice and parsley.
Serve with parmesan.
recipes.notes: Brown the mushrooms properly - that's where the flavour is.

recipes.name: Sweet & Sour Chicken
recipes.method:
Toss the diced chicken in half the cornflour and fry in oil until golden, then set aside.
Stir-fry the chunked peppers and onion for 3 minutes.
Mix ketchup, vinegar, soy, sugar, the pineapple juice from the tin and remaining cornflour.
Add the sauce and pineapple chunks to the pan and bubble until glossy.
Return the chicken and coat.
Serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Better than takeaway and a third of the price.

recipes.name: Beef & Broccoli Noodle Stir-Fry
recipes.method:
Cook the noodles and drain.
Sear the beef strips in very hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli florets with a splash of water for 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, then the soy, oyster sauce and cornflour mixed with a little water.
Return the beef and noodles and toss until glossy.
recipes.notes: Get the pan smoking hot before the beef goes in.

recipes.name: Swedish-Style Meatballs
recipes.method:
Mix both minces with breadcrumbs, egg, grated onion and seasoning, and roll into small balls.
Brown the meatballs in the butter and set aside.
Stir the flour into the pan, then gradually add stock for a smooth gravy.
Add the cream and mustard.
Return the meatballs and simmer 10 minutes.
Serve with mash and greens.
recipes.notes: Lingonberry or cranberry sauce on the side is traditional.

recipes.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.method:
Marinate the diced chicken in the yogurt and half the paste for 20 minutes.
Grill or fry the chicken until charred at the edges.
Soften the diced onions, add garlic and the rest of the paste.
Add passata and simmer 15 minutes, then stir in cream and ground almonds.
Add the chicken and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve with rice.
recipes.notes: The nation's favourite, done properly at home.

recipes.name: Salmon & Creme Fraiche Pasta
recipes.method:
Cook the pasta, adding the peas for the final 2 minutes.
Meanwhile pan-fry the salmon in oil for 3-4 minutes each side, then flake.
Stir the creme fraiche, lemon zest and juice into the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water.
Fold in the salmon and dill gently.
Season and serve.
recipes.notes: Hot-smoked salmon works brilliantly and skips the frying.

recipes.name: Pesto Chicken & Potato Traybake
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Halve the potatoes, toss with oil and roast 15 minutes.
Coat the chicken in most of the pesto and add to the tray.
Roast 30 minutes, adding the tomatoes and green beans for the last 10.
Dot with the remaining pesto to serve.
recipes.notes: One tray, five plates, minimal effort.

recipes.name: Hoisin Pork Stir-Fry
recipes.method:
Cook the noodles and drain.
Slice the pork thinly and stir-fry in hot oil for 3 minutes.
Add the sliced pepper, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the hoisin, soy and a splash of water.
Toss in the noodles and halved pak choi until wilted and coated.
recipes.notes: Slice the pork thin and don't overcook it.

recipes.name: Family Lasagne
recipes.method:
Brown the mince with the diced onion and carrot, add garlic, puree and tomatoes and simmer 30 minutes.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and milk.
Layer ragu, pasta and white sauce in a dish, repeating twice.
Finish with white sauce and grated cheddar.
Bake at 190C for 40 minutes and rest 10 before serving.
recipes.notes: Freezes beautifully in portions - the ultimate batch classic.

recipes.name: Fish Finger Tacos
recipes.method:
Bake the fish fingers per packet until crisp.
Shred the cabbage and toss with the juice of one lime.
Mix the mayonnaise with sriracha and the other lime's juice.
Warm the tortillas.
Build tacos with leaves, cabbage, fish fingers and the spicy mayo.
recipes.notes: Weeknight joy - kids assemble their own.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Souvlaki Bowls
recipes.method:
Marinate the diced chicken in oregano, lemon juice, garlic and half the oil for 20 minutes.
Griddle or fry until charred and cooked through.
Prepare the couscous with boiling water per packet.
Dice the cucumber and halve the tomatoes.
Build bowls with couscous, chicken, salad and a generous spoon of yogurt.
recipes.notes: Add crumbled feta if the budget allows.

recipes.name: Prawn Pad Thai-Style Noodles
recipes.method:
Soak the rice noodles per packet and drain.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar and juice of one lime.
Fry the prawns in hot oil until pink, push aside, and scramble the eggs in the pan.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Add beansprouts and sliced spring onions for 1 minute.
Serve with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.
recipes.notes: Have everything chopped before you start - it moves fast.

recipes.name: Beef Tacos
recipes.method:
Brown the mince with the diced onion in oil.
Add garlic and spices, then the tomatoes, and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Warm the taco shells per packet.
Serve the beef in shells with shredded leaves, grated cheese and soured cream.
recipes.notes: Set everything out and let the table build their own.

recipes.name: Creamy Cajun Chicken Pasta
recipes.method:
Toss the sliced chicken in the cajun seasoning.
Fry in oil until cooked and slightly blackened, then set aside.
Cook the pasta.
Fry the sliced pepper and garlic, add the cream and parmesan to make a sauce.
Return the chicken and toss the pasta through with a splash of pasta water.
recipes.notes: Adjust the cajun to taste - some blends are fiery.

recipes.name: Thai Red Tofu Curry
recipes.method:
Press, cube and fry the tofu in oil until golden, then set aside.
Fry the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the vegetables and cook 6 minutes.
Return the tofu, season with soy and lime juice, and serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Check the paste is vegan if that matters - some contain shrimp.

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Loaded Sweet Potatoes
recipes.method:
Bake the sweet potatoes at 200C for 45-50 minutes until soft.
Poach the chicken for 15 minutes, then shred and mix with the BBQ sauce.
Split the potatoes and pile in the BBQ chicken.
Top with sweetcorn, grated cheese and sliced spring onions.
Finish with soured cream.
recipes.notes: Batch-bake the potatoes and reheat through the week.

recipes.name: Pea & Ham Risotto
recipes.method:
Soften the diced onion and garlic in half the butter.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Stir in the peas and shredded ham for the final 3 minutes.
Beat in the parmesan and remaining butter and rest 2 minutes.
recipes.notes: A great home for leftover gammon.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon Noodles
recipes.method:
Mix the soy, honey, grated ginger and garlic into a teriyaki sauce.
Pan-fry the salmon in oil for 3 minutes each side, add half the sauce and glaze.
Cook the noodles, steaming the broccoli over the same pan.
Toss the noodles and broccoli in the remaining sauce.
Serve the salmon on top, scattered with sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: The glaze thickens fast - keep the heat moderate.

recipes.name: Pork Schnitzel with Quick Slaw
recipes.method:
Bash the pork steaks between cling film until thin.
Coat in flour, beaten egg, then panko.
Shallow-fry for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked.
Shred the cabbage and grate the carrot, then toss with mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Serve the schnitzels with the slaw and lemon wedges.
recipes.notes: Thin and crisp beats thick and chewy - bash them properly.

recipes.name: Turkey Lettuce Wraps (San Choy Bau)
recipes.method:
Fry the turkey mince in oil, breaking it up, until cooked.
Add garlic, ginger and diced water chestnuts for 2 minutes.
Stir in the hoisin and soy.
Separate the lettuce leaves into cups.
Spoon the mince into the leaves and top with sliced spring onions.
recipes.notes: Light, fast and fun to eat with hands.

recipes.name: Toad in the Hole with Onion Gravy
recipes.method:
Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter and rest 20 minutes.
Brown the sausages, then heat the oil in a roasting tin at 220C until smoking.
Add the sausages and pour in the batter.
Bake 30 minutes without opening the door until puffed and golden.
Meanwhile fry the onions slowly in butter, add stock and reduce into gravy.
recipes.notes: A screaming-hot tin is the secret to the rise.

recipes.name: Slow-Roast Lamb Shoulder with Boulangere Potatoes
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 160C.
Slash the lamb, stud with garlic slivers and rosemary, rub with oil and season.
Layer thinly sliced potatoes and onions in a tray, season between layers, and pour over the stock.
Sit the lamb directly on the potatoes and dot with butter.
Roast for 4 hours until the lamb pulls apart and the potatoes have soaked up the juices.
Rest 20 minutes, then serve everything from the tray.
recipes.notes: The potatoes cooking under the lamb are the best part.

recipes.name: Coq au Vin
recipes.method:
Brown the chicken in the butter and set aside.
Fry the lardons, whole peeled shallots and mushrooms until golden.
Add garlic, stir in the flour and tomato puree.
Pour in the wine and stock, return the chicken with the thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 75 minutes.
Uncover for the last 15 minutes to thicken, then serve with mash.
recipes.notes: Use a wine you would happily drink - it is most of the sauce.

recipes.name: King Prawn & Chilli Linguine
recipes.method:
Cook the linguine, reserving a cup of pasta water.
Gently fry the sliced garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the halved tomatoes and wine and bubble 2 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook until just pink.
Toss in the pasta with pasta water, lemon juice and parsley.
recipes.notes: Don't walk away from the prawns - 2 minutes too long ruins them.

recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin with Mustard Cream
recipes.method:
Sear the seasoned tenderloin all over in oil and butter.
Roast at 190C for 18 minutes, then rest under foil.
Fry the diced shallots in the same pan, add wine and reduce by half.
Add stock, cream and mustard and simmer to a sauce.
Boil the potatoes and steam the beans.
Slice the pork and serve with the sauce.
recipes.notes: Tenderloin is lean - resting keeps it juicy.

recipes.name: Proper Roast Chicken Dinner
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C. Butter the chicken, season well, and put the halved lemon and garlic inside.
Roast for 75-90 minutes until the juices run clear, then rest 20 minutes.
Parboil the potatoes, rough them up, and roast in hot oil for 50 minutes.
Roast the carrots alongside and steam the broccoli.
Make gravy from the roasting juices, flour and stock.
Carve and serve everything together.
recipes.notes: Save the carcass for stock - tomorrow's soup is free.

recipes.name: Pan-Seared Scallops with Pea Puree
recipes.method:
Boil the peas for 3 minutes, then blend with the mint, half the butter and a splash of water into a puree.
Fry the lardons until crisp and set aside.
Pat the scallops very dry and season.
Sear in smoking oil for 90 seconds each side, adding butter at the end.
Plate on the pea puree, scatter with lardons and finish with lemon.
recipes.notes: A restaurant-grade starter. Dry scallops are the whole game.

recipes.name: Venison Steaks with Red Wine Jus
recipes.method:
Boil and mash the potatoes with most of the butter.
Sear the seasoned venison in hot oil for 2-3 minutes each side for medium-rare, then rest.
Fry the diced shallots in the pan, add wine and reduce by half.
Add stock and redcurrant jelly and reduce to a glossy jus.
Steam the broccoli.
Serve the sliced venison on mash with the jus.
recipes.notes: Venison is very lean - rare to medium-rare only, and rest it well.

recipes.name: Whole Roast Side of Salmon with Herb Butter
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 190C.
Mash the butter with the chopped herbs, garlic and the zest of one lemon.
Lay the salmon on a lined tray and spread with the herb butter.
Roast for 18-20 minutes until just cooked through.
Boil the potatoes and steam the beans.
Serve the salmon whole at the table with lemon wedges.
recipes.notes: Dramatic to serve, trivially easy to cook.

recipes.name: Beef Bourguignon
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 150C.
Brown the beef in batches in oil and set aside.
Fry the lardons, whole shallots and carrots until coloured, add garlic.
Stir in the flour and puree, then the wine and stock.
Return the beef with the thyme, cover and braise for 2.5 hours.
Fry the mushrooms and stir in for the final 30 minutes.
Serve with mash or crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Better the next day - ideal to make ahead for guests.

recipes.name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Stuffed Chicken

ingredients.name: Soft Cheese with Garlic and Herbs

recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200C.
Cut a pocket into each chicken breast and stuff with the soft cheese and wilted spinach.
Wrap each breast in prosciutto to seal the pocket.
Sear in oil for 2 minutes each side, then roast for 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and steam the broccoli.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, slice and serve.
recipes.notes: The prosciutto bastes the chicken and keeps it moist.

recipes.name: Lamb Kleftiko
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 160C.
Put chunked potatoes, onion wedges, garlic and tomatoes in a deep tray.
Sit the lamb on top, rub with oil, oregano, lemon juice and seasoning.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 3.5 hours.
Uncover, raise to 200C and roast 30 minutes to colour.
Shred the lamb into the juices and serve from the tray.
recipes.notes: Greek holiday food - the sealed tray keeps everything succulent.

recipes.name: Mushroom & Spinach Wellington
recipes.method:
Blitz the mushrooms and fry in butter with the onion, garlic and thyme until completely dry.
Wilt and squeeze the spinach, and crumble in the chestnuts.
Cool the filling completely.
Shape into a log on the pastry, wrap, seal and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200C for 35 minutes until deep golden.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.notes: A vegetarian centrepiece that meat eaters fight over.

recipes.name: Sticky Pork Belly Bao
recipes.method:
Simmer the pork belly in water with the ginger and garlic for 90 minutes, then cool and cube.
Fry the cubes until crisp, then add hoisin, soy and honey and toss until sticky.
Steam the bao buns per packet.
Ribbon the cucumber and slice the spring onions.
Fill the buns with pork, cucumber and spring onion.
recipes.notes: Shop-bought bao buns make this very achievable.

recipes.name: Chicken, Leek & Tarragon Pie
recipes.method:
Brown the diced chicken in half the butter and set aside.
Soften the sliced leeks in the rest, stir in the flour, then the stock for a smooth sauce.
Add the cream, chopped tarragon and chicken and simmer 10 minutes.
Cool slightly, then fill a pie dish.
Top with pastry, crimp, brush with egg and slash a steam hole.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes: Tarragon and chicken is a classic French pairing - don't skip it.

recipes.name: Beef Shin Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 150C.
Brown the beef shin pieces all over in oil and set aside.
Soften the finely diced onion, carrot and celery, add garlic.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then tomatoes and stock.
Return the beef, cover and braise for 3.5 hours until it falls apart.
Shred the beef into the sauce, cook the pappardelle and toss together with parmesan.
recipes.notes: Beef shin is cheap for how luxurious it tastes - the long braise does everything.
